name: Refraction Through Glass Prism Experiment Setup
semanticDescription: Complete assembled laboratory experiment setup for studying refraction and dispersion of light through a triangular glass prism as specified in CBSE Class 10 Physics (NCERT Fig 11.4 & Activity 11.2). Features dual presentation collections: 'Prism_Full' (complete laboratory bench experiment showing wooden board, paper, pins P1/P2, ray box, crown glass prism, and full 7-color VIBGYOR spectral dispersion projected onto an angled observation screen) and 'Prism_Section' (the canonical textbook ray diagram with incident ray PE, refracted ray EF, emergent ray FS, optical pins P1-P4, surface normals NN' and MM', straight-line extensions intersecting at G, and angular arcs for angle of prism A, angle of incidence i, angle of emergence e, and angle of deviation D).
simplifications: Ray beam thickness is slightly exaggerated (1.2mm radius) so that light paths remain distinct and clearly readable across 3D camera angles and educational video renders.
Angle indicator arcs and text notations are included as 3D visual markers for pedagogical clarity.

materials.look: polished laboratory beechwood drawing board with subtle grain texture
bright white matte drawing paper sheet
ultra-clear optical crown glass (Schott N-BK7, IOR 1.517, transmission 0.98)
glowing ruby laser/collimated beam (emission 18.0, pure monochromatic red)
transmitted optical ray inside glass medium with internal glow
deviated emergent light beam exiting into air
luminous gold dashed path marking original incident direction and backward emergent extrapolation
cyan luminous dashed normal lines perpendicular to refracting facets
polished chrome steel pins with crimson spherical heads
amber angular arc highlighting angle of deviation D and angle of prism A
white matte projection screen displaying rainbow spectrum dispersion

interactive_states.label: 1. Apparatus Setup
interactive_states.description: Equilateral glass prism placed on white drawing sheet pinned to wooden bench.

interactive_states.label: 2. White Light Torch On
interactive_states.description: Collimated composite white light beam directed at face AB at incident angle i = 48°.

interactive_states.label: 3. Internal Refraction
interactive_states.description: Light slows down in denser crown glass (n = 1.517) and refracts towards the normal.

interactive_states.label: 4. 7-Color Rainbow Dispersion
interactive_states.description: Rays exit into air and fan out into 7 spectral colors (VIBGYOR) on the observation screen.

cbse_mapping.chapter: Chapter 11: Human Eye and the Colourful World
cbse_mapping.ncert_activity: Activity 11.2 - Refraction of Light Through a Prism
key_formulas: Prism Angle Relation: A + D = i + e
Cauchy's Dispersion Relation: n(λ) = A_c + B_c / λ²
cbse_mapping.exam_takeaways: Violet light (400nm) travels slowest in glass and deviates most (42.6°). Red light (700nm) travels fastest and deviates least (37.8°).
